fact: A Legal 500 guide by a law firm says the Government is preparing a draft AI law with the House of Representatives' Communications and IT Committee, and elsewhere calls it the draft currently before Parliament; the guide gives only its 2026 imprint, so 2026 is used.
The guide says FRA Board Decree No. 57 of 2024, regulating robo-advisors for investment, is AI-specific and requires client suitability assessments and a right to discontinue automated transactions.
The guide states that no binding AI-specific statute is in force in Egypt; its date is the guide's 2026 imprint.

People of Internet says the Draft Artificial Intelligence Law (2024) is moving through stakeholder consultation ahead of expected parliamentary consideration, and that Egypt has no statute naming deepfakes.

El Watan quotes Ahmed Badawi, chair of the House ICT committee, saying the Ministry of Communications is close to finishing a comprehensive AI law draft, to go to the House's third legislative session in January 2026.
MP Sahar Albazar describes a draft AI law with three risk tiers (prohibited, high-risk, limited-risk) that is still progressing towards final legislation.

MP Ahmed Badawi, chair of the House ICT committee, said the ICT ministry is now preparing an integrated AI bill whose outline was agreed in community dialogue sessions, to go to the House once the government finishes it.

Al-Masry Al-Youm reports MP Amira Saber submitted to the House of Representatives a 24-article bill on governance of AI applications, which she calls the first such bill put to the Egyptian parliament.
